blocks.text: *The setting, the artist's unfinished book, and why the world looks the way it does.*

An artist wrote a story in a book and drew its pictures himself — a gentle, peaceful story. Everything he finished is on the page, **drawn flat**. Everyone he has only imagined so far is **unwritten**: real in his mind, not yet on the page.

But unwanted thoughts kept breaking into his mind, and the pictures there grew chaotic. Those thoughts took one shape and one name: **Chaos**. Chaos lives only inside the artist's mind, and it has tried again and again to wreck his peace and his book. It never erases what he wrote — it **corrupts** it.
The world is called *Unwritten* for the people still waiting to be written — and you are one of them.

To fight Chaos the artist imagined fourteen champions, the **Fourteen Kashira**. Together they struck it down and sealed it away — or believed they had — but not before it **corrupted pages of the book**, twisting the characters drawn on them into monsters.

**The seal closed on an empty shell.** In the battle's last moments Chaos slipped into one of the Fourteen — **Veyra**, the Sword — and walked home among them wearing her face. **Morwen**, the Scythe, saw it and said so; Veyra accused her back, and most of the Fourteen believed the hero over the curse-caster. The artist could not tell which of his champions was lying, so he doubted every one of them, until his fear turned all fourteen into the **fourteen shadows**. Thirteen of them are innocent. Chaos lives in one. Now only the unwritten stand with him. You are one of them, and your task is to end that fear: restore the corrupted pages, remember the Fourteen one by one until each is proven, and in the end face the shadow where Chaos truly lives. The whole battle is told in **The Whole Story**.
Nothing about how Unwritten looks is arbitrary. The visual style *is* the story:

items: **The flat, papery monsters are corrupted pages.** They are literally paper — drawings Chaos twisted. Their flatness isn't an art choice; it's what they are.

**The colorless, charcoal heroes are the unwritten.** The body is 3D and fully present, but the artist hasn't put them on the page yet — no color, no self. A faint trace of identity is already there: a hint of colored hair, an inked eye.
**Beating a monster restores its page.** What it drops is what the page gives back.

blocks.text: Progression in Unwritten is the story of **getting your color.** The more of you is written — growing stronger, journeying further, uncovering story, mastering a weapon — the more **color returns to you**, identity arriving for the first time. A fully realized hero is one the artist has written a great deal of.

The artist gave every one of the Fourteen a **name**, but never wrote one on the page — their names are spoken, never written. Each is also called by the **style** they fought in: *the Blossom Wind Kashira* is Veyra.

items: **Each of the fourteen weapons is one of them.** A weapon is what the artist kept of a Kashira from before they fell. How the weapon fights *is* how that Kashira fought.

**A weapon teaches its wielder's skills in fragments.** As your mastery of that kind of weapon grows, you choose which of them to draw out — and a weapon forged by a smith carries one of them more strongly than the rest: its **trademark**, the skill it is named for.

**Remembering who they really were frees the artist.** Every Kashira you come to know through their weapon proves to him that Chaos never had them — and remembering the real Veyra proves that the shadow wearing her face is not her. Master whichever weapons you like — nobody has to learn all fourteen.
**Carrying one bleeds their identity into you** — this is the charcoal-to-color return. You are not recovering *the* truth; you are finishing *a* story.

**Writing a Kashira's name back into the book is the endgame.** Learn enough of a weapon's skills and its Kashira's name can finally be put on the page — fourteen names to write, fourteen journeys to finish.

blocks.text: Read top to bottom, their legends are the battle in brief.

rows: When Chaos first came, Celestia drifted above it like a cloud nobody could catch, and rained arrows on it until it turned to chase her.
It chased her straight into Orion, who caught it the way a river catches a falling branch, and bent its path to where the others waited.
There Mordane rose like a raging tide, and one swing swept its whole front off the road.
What survived lunged at Orion, until Tharos leapt and brought his hammer down hard enough to break a falling star. The earth split open beneath it, and the whole field froze mid-breath.
Asterion stepped in front of the others, took every blow meant for them, then spent everything he had on one fist that lit the sky like the northern lights.
Through that light Varkhaz charged, never once stepping back, each blow catching the next like wildfire in dry grass.

Veyra dashed past him into the very heart of it and cut it a thousand times in a few heartbeats. The heart died, and as it died Chaos fled into the one who had killed it. Veyra fell before the petals settled.
Seraphine ran to her through the storm. As the morning mist settled over her, Veyra opened her eyes and stood, and Seraphine felt something cold look back at her. She said nothing.
The dark, empty now but still moving, split into a hundred shapes, and Riven answered with a hundred blades, whirling through them like leaves in an autumn gale.
In the confusion nobody saw Velmora arrive. She nicked it once with a blade dark with nightshade, and stepped back to let the poison bloom.
As it seemed to weaken, Kaelen set the ground beneath it burning, then froze the fire to ash under ice, so it had nowhere left to stand.

Only Morwen saw what the others missed: her curse on the dark never took hold, because nothing was inside it, and Veyra's petals had stopped falling. Telling no one yet, she laid a second, slower curse on Veyra.
Nysara circled unseen, a mirage in the dust, until one crack showed, then struck that same spot again and again until it split wide.

For three moonless nights Vael had lain still on the farthest hill. Through Nysara's crack he fired one shot out of the dark, and the seal closed. Fourteen walked home. But the seal had closed on an empty shell, and Chaos walked home with them, wearing Veyra's face.

blocks.text: The great powers of the world

items: **Chaos** — the unwanted thoughts in the artist's mind. It never erases; it corrupts. The Fourteen believed they sealed it away; it walked home with them instead, wearing Veyra's face.
**The fourteen shadows** — the Kashira, turned by the artist's fear. Thirteen are his fear wearing his champions' shapes, and they come back whenever the fear does. The fourteenth is Chaos itself.
**The corrupted pages** — the monsters of the world, and the reason to keep walking.
